Hands-on Lab 56: Build an end-to-end data product
Prerequisites

Disposable local or cloud sandbox with budgets and expiry controls.

Git, containers, Kubernetes or a documented simulation as appropriate.

Synthetic identities and data only; do not use employer or customer secrets.

Implementation
1. Define fictional requirements, users, ownership and acceptance criteria for dataops portfolio project.
2. Create the smallest safe implementation or detailed simulation using Kafka, Airflow, dbt, OpenLineage.
3. Add identity, policy, metadata, telemetry, quota, cost and lifecycle controls.
4. Run one successful user journey and one intentionally denied action.
5. Inject a bounded dependency or configuration failure, diagnose it, recover and record the timeline.
6. Publish a sanitized architecture, runbook, evidence pack and improvement backlog; then clean up all
resources. Validation Evidence

Architecture and service contract committed to version control.

Commands, test results, screenshots or exported telemetry for allow, deny and failure scenarios.

Recovery, cost, ownership, security and cleanup evidence with timestamps. Interview Questions and Model Answers
1. How would you design DataOps Portfolio Project?
Begin with consumers, outcomes, constraints and ownership. Define the service contract and failure
boundaries, choose the minimum viable architecture, automate policy and lifecycle, then prove normal,
denied and recovery behavior.
2. Which trade-offs would you document?
Document speed versus control, abstraction versus transparency, standardization versus flexibility,
managed service versus portability, centralization versus team autonomy, and cost versus resilience.
3. What production evidence is required?
Require version-controlled architecture and configuration, effective-access results, policy tests, user-journey
telemetry, SLOs, rollback or restore evidence, ownership, cost allocation and a clean teardown or
deprecation path.

telemetry, SLOs, rollback or restore evidence, ownership, cost allocation and a clean teardown or
deprecation path.

Use developer research, remove the largest friction, ship a narrow golden path, publish support and escape
hatches, measure time-to-value and satisfaction, and iterate with representative product teams. Chapter Summary

DataOps Portfolio Project is an owned product or operating capability, not a one-time installation.

Enterprise readiness requires explicit contracts, boundaries, policy, telemetry and lifecycle controls.



